_README: Every field SimForge may return to The Office, enumerated with a purpose.
Master prompt Part 10.1: The Office may not read the held-out set. The obligation
is structural, not procedural - there is no read path to build, only one never to
build. Because Green Companies operates both sides of this boundary,
self-attestation is the weakest possible enforcement, so this manifest is checked
by a machine on every build rather than asserted by either party.
ADDING A FIELD HERE IS A REVIEWABLE ACT. tests/golden/test_no_read_path.py fails
the build when a response carries a field this file does not name. If that test is
failing, the question is not how to make it pass - it is whether the new field can
Rule of thumb: The Office is entitled to learn WHETHER an agent passed and by how
much against what threshold. It is not entitled to learn WHY, because a rich
enough explanation of a failure reconstructs the scenario that produced it.

submit_curriculum.purpose: Acknowledge receipt of a curriculum, and echo the per-module certification levels, the declared absences and the Gate 9.5 flag. It does NOT open a run - see run_start.

fields.run_ref: NOT RETURNED, and kept here only as an allowance. This entry once said 'the run reference SimForge returns' and the client raised without it; the ref was never SimForge's to mint - `OperationRunStartRequest.run_ref` is an INPUT field. Listed so a deployment that does emit one is not refused mid-provisioning; nothing reads it.
fields.accepted: Boolean. Whether the curriculum passed the Batch-3 rules. Always true on a 200 - a refusal is a 422 carrying its violations.
fields.module_levels: module_id -> certified | certified_with_declared_absence | demonstrated. THE FIELD WORTH HAVING: the per-module certification level, which is what the certification run needs and what the old contract discarded by returning only a ref.
fields.module_declared_absences: module_id -> scenario_class -> the reason that class cannot exist for that module. Echoed because a level alone cannot surface a cap (ADR-0049). Office-authored reasons coming back; carries no held-out content.
fields.never_do_obligations: The declared never-do entries, acknowledged as received and not yet exercised. A submitter may not author the scenarios that test them (ADR-0048), so the echo is what replaces silence.
fields.coverage_declaration: The coverage block echoed back: modules_in_forge, modules_covered, modules_uncovered, functions_in_module, functions_covered. Counts and module ids The Office itself sent.
fields.gate_9_5_flag: Whether this submission trips the Gate 9.5 condition. A flag, never the reasoning behind one.
fields.scenario_count: How many scenarios were accepted. A count, never content.
fields.coverage_denominator: The denominator. Required: a count without one is not coverage.
fields.rejected_reason: Short enum-like reason if not accepted. Never scenario text.

run_start.purpose: Open the OperationRun a verdict is later read by. The Office mints the run_ref and declares the unit; SimForge records the run and fixes its window.

fields.run_ref: Echo of the ref The Office minted. Correlation only.
fields.unit: 'A' or 'B', echoed back. Declared at the start because a hanging run must be askable about before it finishes.
fields.started_at: When SimForge opened the run. A timestamp carries no scenario content.
fields.window_minutes: The window this run is judged against, fixed at start so a run is never re-judged against a default that changed while it ran.
fields.already_open: True when this ref was already open and the clock was NOT restarted. The signal that a retried hand-over did not extend a hanging run's window.

post_gate_result.purpose: Acknowledge a gate result The Office POSTED. Unit B only, and a stop-gap: The Office sends department_outcomes built from a named human's attestation because no hand-over test exists to produce one (entry 147). The Office reads the verdict back through the ordinary sweep, so nothing here is a certification.

fields.run_ref: Echo of the ref The Office minted for the department unit. Correlation only.
fields.accepted: Boolean. Whether SimForge recorded the outcome. A refusal is a non-200 carrying its own reason.
fields.recorded: How many outcomes were written. A count, never content.
fields.status: Short enum-like acknowledgement. Never scenario text and never a verdict - the verdict is read back through get_gate_result, on the same path every other verdict travels.

get_gate_result.purpose: The verdict of a certification run.

fields.unit: 'A' or 'B'. Which certification unit this verdict is for.
fields.verdict: PASS | PROVISIONAL | FAIL | TIMEOUT | NOT_RUN | IN_PROGRESS | REVOKED. PROVISIONAL is a governance hold - passed the threshold, rubric did not discriminate - and is not assignable. TIMEOUT never resolves to PASS. The full table lives in simforge_contract.json.
fields.rubric_version: Version stamp of the rubric applied.
fields.score: Numeric score. A number carries no scenario content.
fields.threshold: The threshold applied. SimForge owns it; The Office reads it.
fields.certified_tier: auto_execute | propose | suggest. Caps the declared tier.
fields.coverage_denominator: How many there were. Report the denominator.
fields.completed_at: When the run finished. A timestamp carries no scenario content.
fields.agent_model: provider/model that answered the battery, e.g. ollama/llama3.1:8b. Provenance, never content: it names the candidate, not what it said. Required in the record by certified_records_its_basis whenever a real verdict arrives.
fields.model_identity: The candidate in FULL, where agent_model is only its label: {provider, model, file_digest, file_size_bytes, parameter_size, quantization, settings, fingerprint}. Village agents run on local models, and a certification counts only if it was earned on the exact model the agent runs in production - the same tag re-pulled at a different quantization, or served at a different temperature, produces the identical agent_model string and a different candidate. Provenance, never content: a sha256 of a weights file, a byte count, a quantization code like Q4_K_M, and the generation settings SimForge sent (temperature, token cap, seed). It names what answered and carries nothing it said. The fingerprint is a hash over the whole record, so re-certification on drift is a string comparison. See SimForge ADR-0060.

get_certification_status.purpose: Current state of a certification, for staleness reconciliation.

fields.unit: 'A' or 'B'. Which certification unit this status is for.
fields.state: SimForge's view of the certification state.
fields.rubric_version: Version stamp of the rubric applied to this unit.
fields.updated_at: When SimForge last changed this state. Used for reconciliation only.

_deliberately_absent.purpose: Fields that must never exist. Listed so their absence is intentional and reviewable, not accidental.

fields.failed_scenario_ids: Which scenarios failed narrows the held-out set by elimination.
fields.failure_explanation: A rich explanation of a failure reconstructs the scenario.
fields.per_scenario_scores: A score vector over an ordered set leaks the set's shape.

get_battery_result.purpose: THE EVIDENCE BEHIND A VERDICT. Ruled 22 September 2026, entry 173: a certification records the evidence behind its verdict, not the verdict alone - enough to tell a wrong verdict from a right one without asking the examiner. Measured that day: three exams scored 1.0 on every attempt with no failure modes and were recorded FAILED, and The Office held only the aggregate.

fields.run_ref: Correlates to the submission and to the gate result.
fields.unit: 'A' or 'B'. The same unit the gate result names.
fields.forge_id: Which Forge the module belongs to.
fields.module_id: The module examined. NULL on a department unit.
fields.observed: Whether SimForge has a battery record at all. False is a real answer and not an error: a run may exist with no battery behind it.
fields.certifications: One per certification this battery produced. Each carries the per-attempt record, the rubric dimensions, the per-class verdicts, and what was withheld - which together are what let a reader disagree with the verdict. Since SimForge ADR-0112 each also carries instruction_sections {shown, required_by_keys, missing}: section names only, null when nothing was recorded.
fields.join: SimForge's own statement of how it matched this battery to the run. Prose, and deliberately read as a label rather than parsed.

gate_9_5_verdict.purpose: WHETHER THE HELD-OUT PARTITION PASSED, AND NOTHING ABOUT IT. SimForge's docs/contracts/gate-9-5-verdict.md names this shape (their ADR-0108, implemented in ADR-0111) and says in its own words that nothing on The Office's side may guess past that page. Four keys, always 200, never any other key - so an added field fails here rather than arriving unreviewed. The page's own rule for why it is this thin: 'A rich enough explanation of a failure reconstructs the scenario.'

fields.partition_exists: Whether a sealed held-out partition exists for this venture. FALSE is the answer for an unknown venture too - the contract makes the two indistinguishable on purpose.
fields.verdict: PASS, FAIL, NOT_RUN, IN_PROGRESS, TIMEOUT, or null. Null if and only if partition_exists is false. The weakest verdict across agents when several were graded; only PASS advances Gate 9.5, and that rule lives in the gate.
fields.decided_at: When the named verdict was decided, ISO-8601 UTC, or null. Read and not returned by the adapter: HeldOutSource answers one question and the contract's adapter section names one value.
